features.heading: Image Compression with a Quality Setting You Control
features.intro: Need to compress image online? Select one local JPG, PNG, or WebP file, choose the quality level, and download a separate WebP result when you are ready.

items.title: Control the balance between file size and detail
items.description: Choose a setting from 35% to 90% based on how you plan to use the image. Start higher when fine edges or texture matter, then compare the downloaded WebP with your source file before you replace anything.

image.alt: Quality control illustration with no text

items.title: Keep the selected image in this browser
items.description: The image you choose is processed locally in this browser for this tool. It is not uploaded to Streamnest servers, so you can complete the compression task from the same page.

image.alt: Local browser processing illustration with no text

items.title: Save a separate WebP result
items.description: Start with a JPG, PNG, or WebP file and download a new WebP result. Your original file is not overwritten, giving you a straightforward way to compare the two versions before use.

image.alt: Image result workflow illustration with no text

items.title: Choose a local image
items.body: Select a JPG, PNG, or WebP image within the 50 MB allowance.

items.title: Adjust the quality
items.body: Choose a setting from 35% to 90%. Lower settings can create a smaller result, but they can also reduce visible detail.

items.title: Save and review
items.body: Download the WebP result, then compare its appearance and file size with the original before you use it.

items.title: An Image Size Compressor Works Through a Trade-off
items.body: An image size compressor reduces the bytes needed for a new file. With this tool, the quality setting lets you choose the balance between file size and visible detail. A lower setting can soften fine texture, edges, and other details, so evaluate the downloaded WebP at the size where you plan to use it.

items.title: What “Image Compress” Means Here
items.body: “Image compress” is a common shorthand for creating a smaller image file. Here, the selected JPG, PNG, or WebP image becomes a separate WebP result. An image that has already been optimized may stay close to its original size.

items.title: Output Format
items.body: This tool saves WebP. If you need another available output format after saving the result, use Image Converter.

supporting.heading: When to Use This Image Compressor

items.body: Create a separate WebP version of a JPG, PNG, or WebP image for a website, message, or upload form.
Try a quality setting when file size matters and inspect the new result before replacing the source.
Keep the original file intact while you decide whether the WebP result is the version you want to share.

items.question: What image formats can I compress?
items.answer: Choose a JPG, PNG, or WebP image up to 50 MB. The downloaded result is WebP.

items.question: Can I compress an image without losing quality?
items.answer: The tool provides a 35%–90% quality setting. Lower settings can reduce visible detail, so compare the downloaded WebP with the original before you replace anything.

items.question: Can I save a compressed JPG instead?
items.answer: No. This compressor produces WebP. Use Image Converter if another available output format is needed after download.

items.question: Is my image uploaded to Streamnest?
items.answer: No. The selected image is processed locally in this browser for this tool and is not uploaded to Streamnest servers.

items.question: How can I compress an image online?
items.answer: Choose a supported local image, adjust the quality setting, then download the separate WebP result. Keep the tab open while the result is created.

items.question: Is Image Compressor free?
items.answer: Yes. Image Compressor is a free browser-local tool.
